name: AHT20 temperature & humidity sensor
description: Aosong (ASAIR) digital temperature (-40 to 85 °C, ±0.3 °C typical) and relative humidity (0–100 %, ±2 % typical) sensor with an I2C interface and a CRC-checked 20-bit reading. Sold as: AHT20 breakout (4-pin: VIN, GND, SCL, SDA), fixed I2C address 0x38.
eli5: Tells your board how warm the air is and how damp it is.

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Supply, 2.7–5.5 V (use the same voltage as your board's logic, 3.3 V on ESP32/Pico)

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (10 kΩ pull-up on the breakout)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (10 kΩ pull-up on the breakout)

supplierQuery: AHT20 temperature humidity sensor breakout I2C
buildNotes: Wait at least 100 ms after power-on, then read one status byte: bit 3 set means calibrated; if it is clear send 0xBE 0x08 0x00 and wait 10 ms.
Measure: send 0xAC 0x33 0x00, wait 80 ms, read until status bit 7 (busy) is clear, then read 7 bytes: status, 20-bit humidity, 20-bit temperature, CRC.
Check the CRC (poly 0x31, init 0xFF over the first 6 bytes). A mismatch almost always means a loose SDA/SCL wire.
The address is fixed at 0x38, so only one AHT20 per I2C bus.
Power VIN from the same voltage as the microcontroller's logic (3.3 V on ESP32/Pico): the SDA/SCL pull-ups go to VIN.
Keep the sensor away from the board's regulator and the microcontroller, which warm the air around them.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from aht20 import AHT20

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
sensor = AHT20(i2c)
while True:
    t, h = sensor.read()
    print('T=%.1fC H=%.0f%%' % (t, h))
    time.sleep(1)
